title: No single cause for a many-cause system
statement: In science content, never present one factor as the sole driver or fix of a system with several causes; name the other causes and the uncertainty.
detail: A red-team factual pass of a Grade 3 reading corpus, checked against agency sources, found lessons that made one factor the whole story: returning wolves said to have reversed and fixed a forest's damage, where the park service describes wolves as one contributor in a debated, multi-factor system, and the sun called the single engine of the water cycle, where the geological survey says solar energy and gravity drive water's movement. A Grade 5 generation contract's science rule says one local food-web pattern or intervention does not guarantee a universal population response, biodiversity effect or recovery, and asks for the condition, the direct and indirect pathways, alternative stressors, site scope and uncertainty to be stated. No effect on learners is recorded.

evidence.quote: - U5-L5 says returning Yellowstone wolves "reversed" and "fixed" the damage and proves one predator keeps a forest healthy. NPS describes wolves as one contributor in a debated, multi-factor system involving other predators, hunting, water, drought, and climate ([NPS](https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/cyclesprocesses.htm)).

- U6-L2 calls the sun the single water-cycle engine and wind the single force. USGS says solar energy **and gravity** drive water's movement ([USGS](https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-earths-water-cycle)).
